people.notes: 3rd daughter of John McKeil Anderson and Mary Ricketts Van Cortlandt. Mary was a daughter of Philip Van Cortlandt (1734-1814) of the Dutch/American Van Cortlandt family of New York, America. He was a "Loyalist" at the time of the American War of Independence and was disinherited by his family. Among his ancestors was Stephanus Van Cortland (1643-1700?), the first native born Mayor of New York City (1677). Catherine died at Ootacamundt in 1863 Inscribed tomb in St Stephen's Churchyard, Ooty. India.

people.death: 1857 Jun 27th, in the massacre at Cawnpore.
people.notes: Born at Karnal 6 Oct 1826. Educated by Dr Grieg of Leytonstone and at Addiscombe (1843-4). Returned to India "overland" 1845. Ensign 16th Bengal Native Infantry 10 Feb 1846, Lieutenant 6 Jan 1850. Faced General Court Martial at Dinapore 25 Oct 1847 for "unbecoming conduct", sentenced to "severe reprimand". Killed in the massacre at Cawnpore 27 June 1857. Married in Benares 31 Oct 1850 Memorial in All Saints Church Cawnpore.

Born London 26 Jan 1800. Cadet 1819. Admitted 14 June 1820. Cornet 10 Jan 1820. Lieutenant 14 Aug 1822. Captain 26 Aug 1831. Major 26 July 1841. Invalided 28 Sept 1841. Died Ootacamund 22 Jan 1869. Service: joined GG's Bodyguard 1820, posted as Cornet to 7th Light Cavalry 1821, Adjutant 7th LC 1825-26, Deputy Judge Advocate General Dinapore & Benares divisions 1832-1840 (also Sirhind Division 1835). Judge Advocate General to the Army of the Indus at Ferozapore during 1st Afghan War 1838-39. Married 15 December 1825.

people.profession: Master of Equitation & Fencing to - among many others - Frederick Prince of Wales

people.notes: With her two daughters was among the last Europeans to leave Cawnpore before the siege. Her eldest daughter, Helena, was born at Etawah on June 22 1853 and her youngest child, Frederick, was born at Calcutta after the death of his father

people.profession: Cadet 1778. Sailed to India on the 'Gratton' in 1778. Ensign 1778. Lieutenant in Cavalry 1778. Resigned 1785. Served in Governor General's Bodyguard 1780-81. Appointed ridingmaster to the Bengal army on monthly salary of Rs1500.

people.notes: Served with distinction as a General in the armies of both Ranjit Singh and the EIC. For the latter raised a regiment of levies which subsequently became the 23rd Punjab Infantry.
Founder of the branch of the family that settled on land now known as van C. Park NYC.

people.profession: Alderman & member of Governors Council, active merchant,  aquired additional city property including a coffee house & a tavern,The Fighting Cocks.

Soldier, Judge of the Court of Admiralty, Judge of Superior Court of Pleas of Kings County, Associate Judge & later Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of the Province of New York,  Justice of the Court of Oyer & Terminer, Chancellor of the Court of Chancery. Served on  the Governor's Council under both Dutch & English. Mayor of New York City, Commissioner of Customs & Collector of Revenue, Secretary of the Province of  New York. Brewer & businessman. Landowner.
people.notes: First native born Mayor of New York, 1677

Educated at University of London. Appointed to Bengal Civil Service after competative exam of 1866. Arrived India Dec 10 1868 and served in NW Provinces in various grades as Collector & Magistrate. Retired in August 1893. Married at Mynpoorie Dec 12th 1870. Died Grayswood, Haslemere 1926.

people.profession: Manager of ANGELO Brothers (Merchants) in Calcutta.
